History

The silicone ashtray with a lid is the newest ashtray form in this lane, because it only became possible when food-grade silicone rubber became cheap enough for everyday goods in the 2010s. Silicone ashtrays were first sold as unbreakable travel ashtrays: soft, light, and impossible to shatter, with a lid that closed over the bowl to keep ash in and smell down. The lid turned the ashtray into a pocket object, and makers added windproof lids, odour seals, and folding forms, until silicone became the majority of premium unbreakable ashtray production. Over time the same basic form was copied, adapted, and refined by many makers, so the record today covers a family of closely related objects rather than a single patented shape. The sources cited at the end of this record give the reader places to check each stage, and the history matters because it explains why the parts are arranged the way they are: each feature survives because it solved a practical problem for the people who used the supply every day.

The supply in detail

The silicone ashtray with lid works by giving ash and spent material a soft rubber dish to land in, with a lid that closes over the bowl to keep ash in, keep wind out, and keep smell down. It is made from food-grade silicone rubber, and a common example measures about 100 mm across and 28 mm deep, with a 4 mm wall and a lid 104 mm across and 5 mm thick, holding about 186 cubic centimetres of ash and debris. The silicone tolerates heat up to about 230 degrees C, it cannot break if dropped, and it washes clean in a dishwasher. The lid seals by contact: a lip on the lid presses into the rim of the dish, and the soft rubber gives enough to seal without a gasket. The parts fit together in a fixed order, and each part has one job: to hold the material, to apply the mechanism, or to carry the result to the user. Because the parts are simple and the mechanism is mechanical rather than electronic in its basic form, the supply can be understood by inspection, measured with a ruler, and checked by the arithmetic in this record.

Parts and variants

Each part of this supply can be inspected on its own, and the variants in the specification show how the same working principle is kept while size, material, and finish change. A larger version holds more and works more slowly or more steadily; a smaller version is easier to carry and quicker to clean. Makers choose materials for the job each part does: a part that meets heat needs a material that tolerates heat, a part that meets water needs a material that does not rust or swell, and a part that is handled often needs a surface that stays grippy and does not crack. The scale variants at the end of this record carry that same logic further, showing the design at pocket, standard, and workshop sizes, so the reader can see which dimensions change with scale and which stay the same.

Spec

Materials: Food-grade silicone rubber; heat tolerance about 230 degrees C; no metal or plastic in the ash path

Dimensions: Dish 100 mm across and 28 mm deep; wall 4 mm thick; lid 104 mm across and 5 mm thick; about 124 grams total

Mechanism: Ash and spent material fall into the soft rubber dish; rim rests hold a cigarette or joint by gravity; the lid lip seals by contact to keep ash in and smell down

Use: Set on a flat surface, rest the cigarette in a rim rest, tap ash into the dish, close the lid when the session ends or wind picks up, empty when ash reaches a third of the depth

Care: Wash with warm soapy water or in a dishwasher; do not leave a lit ember pressed against one spot; check the lid lip for wear and replace the lid if it no longer seals

Variants: Round and square dishes; hinged and loose lids; folding travel forms; plain and glow colours; pocket and table sizes

Materials and design

The silicone ashtray is a rubber design, and the choice is food-grade silicone against cheaper general-purpose rubber. Food-grade silicone is chosen here because it tolerates heat to about 230 degrees C without giving off fumes, it does not hold smell, and it is safe to wash in a dishwasher, while cheaper rubber softens, smells, and can melt.

Build it yourself

A silicone ashtray with a lid is a genuine home build, and this record gives it in full, because casting silicone in a mould is a real do-it-yourself craft. Start with a bought two-part food-grade silicone rubber kit, the kind sold for mould making, and a mould: either a bought ashtray mould or a home mould made by pressing a bought glass ashtray, 100 mm across, into a box of modelling clay to form the cavity.

3D printing

The silicone ashtray with lid is printable in TPU on a home printer, and this record gives the full directions, because TPU is the flexible filament that behaves most like silicone rubber. Print the dish and lid in 95A TPU, which is soft enough to seal and firm enough to hold its shape, with a 0.4 mm nozzle, a 0.2 mm layer height, 15 percent gyroid infill, and 4 perimeters, giving a wall about 1.6 mm thick.

Use and program

To use the silicone ashtray with lid, set it on a flat surface, rest the cigarette or joint in a rim rest between draws, and tap ash into the dish. Close the lid when the session ends or when wind picks up, and the seal will keep ash in and smell down.

Science proof

A silicone ashtray works by heat tolerance, elasticity, and a contact seal. Silicone rubber tolerates continuous heat up to about 230 degrees C, the figure the cited supplier guides give, because its silicon-oxygen backbone does not break down the way a carbon backbone does, so a hot ember on the surface chars the ash but not the dish. Its density is near 1.15 grams per cubic centimetre and its specific heat near 1.46 joules per gram per kelvin, so a dish and lid of about 124 grams store roughly 36,200 joules when heated by 200 kelvin, and its thermal conductivity is low, so the outside stays cool to touch while the inside takes the heat. Silicone is elastic, so the lid lip stretches over the rim and springs back to seal, and it is non-porous, so tar and smell sit on the surface instead of soaking in. The dish is a shallow cylinder, so its capacity is pi times radius squared times depth, and the lid is a flat disc whose volume is pi times radius squared times thickness. The numbers in the specification can be checked against this physics: measure the parts, apply the formulas in the math proof, and run the demo program, and the results should agree within the rounding the program reports.

Math proof

The demo treats the dish and the lid as cylinders. With a dish diameter of 100.0 mm and a depth of 28.0 mm, the inner diameter is 92.0 mm, so the capacity is pi times 46 squared times 28, about 186,133 cubic millimetres, or 186.13 cubic centimetres. The outer cylinder is 100.0 mm across and 32.0 mm tall, counting the 4 mm base, about 251,327 cubic millimetres, leaving a body shell of 65.19 cubic centimetres, and at a silicone density of 1.15 grams per cubic centimetre the body mass is 74.97 grams. The lid is 104.0 mm across and 5.0 mm thick, so its volume is pi times 52 squared times 5, about 42.47 cubic centimetres, and its mass is 48.85 grams. The total mass is 123.82 grams, and multiplying by the specific heat of 1.46 and a 200 kelvin rise gives about 36,155 joules of stored heat. Every number comes from the specification in this record, the formulas are shown in full, and the program prints each quantity so the reader can check the arithmetic. The computation runs twice with SHA-256 digests printed, so the reader can confirm it is deterministic.

Use and care

Set on a flat surface, rest the cigarette in a rim rest, tap ash into the dish, close the lid when the session ends or wind picks up, empty when ash reaches a third of the depth Wash with warm soapy water or in a dishwasher; do not leave a lit ember pressed against one spot; check the lid lip for wear and replace the lid if it no longer seals

Legal note

Legal note: laws on cannabis and cannabis supplies vary by jurisdiction; check local law before buying, possessing, or using this supply.

Sources

  • Accio — Premium Ashtrays with Lids — https://www.accio.com/plp/ashtray-with-lid — Ashtrays with lids are judged by lid seal effectiveness, heat resistance, ease of emptying, and wind resistance; silicone units use food-grade silicone, and heat resistance of at least 200 degrees C is a selection benchmark.
  • Sovol — TPU 3D Printing Guide — https://www.sovol3d.com/blogs/news/tpu-3d-printing-guide-best-settings-for-flexible-parts-without-stringing-or-jams — A safe starting profile for 95A TPU: nozzle 220-235 degrees C, bed 40-60 degrees C, layer height 0.20-0.24 mm with a 0.4 mm nozzle, infill 10-25% gyroid or lines, retraction 0.6-1.2 mm direct drive.
build_yourself: A silicone ashtray with a lid is a genuine home build, and this record gives it in full, because casting silicone in a mould is a real do-it-yourself craft. Start with a bought two-part food-grade silicone rubber kit, the kind sold for mould making, and a mould: either a bought ashtray mould or a home mould made by pressing a bought glass ashtray, 100 mm across, into a box of modelling clay to form the cavity. Mix the two silicone parts in equal measure by weight, stir slowly for three minutes to avoid trapping air, and pour the mix into the mould from a low height so it flows into the rim notches. Tap the mould on the table to bring air bubbles to the surface, and let it cure for 24 hours at room temperature without moving it. For the lid, pour a second, thinner mix into a flat mould, a 104 mm circle cut from a plastic tub lid, with a 5 mm spacer ring to set the thickness, and let it cure the same way. When both parts are cured, peel them from their moulds, trim any flash with scissors, wash them in warm soapy water, and check the lid lip against the dish rim: it should press on with a light push and lift off with one hand. That cast dish and lid are the build, and they work because the silicone is the same food-grade rubber the bought form uses.

demo.code:
"""Demo: silicone ashtray and lid volumes and heat storage — The Silicone Ashtray with Lid."""
import hashlib, math
def compute():
    d = 100.0; h = 28.0; wall = 4.0; lid_d = 104.0; lid_t = 5.0; rho = 1.15; cp = 1.46; dT = 200.0
    cap_mm3 = math.pi * ((d - 2.0 * wall) / 2.0) ** 2 * h
    cap_cm3 = cap_mm3 / 1000.0
    outer_mm3 = math.pi * (d / 2.0) ** 2 * (h + wall)
    body_cm3 = (outer_mm3 - cap_mm3) / 1000.0
    body_g = body_cm3 * rho
    lid_mm3 = math.pi * (lid_d / 2.0) ** 2 * lid_t
    lid_cm3 = lid_mm3 / 1000.0
    lid_g = lid_cm3 * rho
    total_g = body_g + lid_g
    heat_J = total_g * cp * dT
    return {"capacity_mm3": round(cap_mm3, 2), "capacity_cm3": round(cap_cm3, 2), "body_volume_cm3": round(body_cm3, 2), "body_mass_g": round(body_g, 2), "lid_volume_cm3": round(lid_cm3, 2), "lid_mass_g": round(lid_g, 2), "total_mass_g": round(total_g, 2), "heat_to_200C_J": round(heat_J, 2)}
def main():
    a = compute(); b = compute()
    sa = hashlib.sha256(repr(sorted(a.items())).encode()).hexdigest()
    sb = hashlib.sha256(repr(sorted(b.items())).encode()).hexdigest()
    for key in ['capacity_mm3', 'capacity_cm3', 'body_volume_cm3', 'body_mass_g', 'lid_volume_cm3', 'lid_mass_g', 'total_mass_g', 'heat_to_200C_J']:
        print(f"{key}: {a[key]}")
    print(f"Run 1 SHA-256: {sa}")
    print(f"Run 2 SHA-256: {sb}")
    print(f"Deterministic: {'MATCH' if sa == sb else 'MISMATCH'}")
if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

materials_design: The silicone ashtray is a rubber design, and the choice is food-grade silicone against cheaper general-purpose rubber. The wall is 4 mm thick, which is the working compromise: thinner walls are lighter and fold flat but let heat through to the table, thicker walls insulate better and hold their shape but make the dish stiff and hard to empty. The lid is 5 mm thick with a lip that presses into the rim, and its tolerance is the lip diameter, sized to stretch over the rim and spring back to seal without a gasket. The rim rests are moulded into the dish wall, so they cannot come loose, and their tolerance is the width of the cut, sized to hold a cigarette without letting it roll. The finish is matte silicone in plain or glow colours, and the design varies by dish size, by lid type, hinged or loose, and by whether the dish folds flat for travel, while the working principle stays the same.

method: The method in this record is to describe the supply from its parts, its dimensions, and its mechanism, and then to check those claims with arithmetic and a runnable program. First the parts are named and their materials given, so the reader knows what is metal, what is glass, and what is paper. Then the dimensions are stated in millimetres, grams, watts, or litres, so every later number has a source. Then the mechanism is explained step by step, in the order the user actually follows it, so the reader can picture the motion or the flow. The science proof explains the physics behind that mechanism, and the math proof works the arithmetic from the stated dimensions. Finally the demo program computes the same quantities from the same numbers, prints them with units, and runs twice with SHA-256 digests, so the reader can repeat the whole check on their own machine without trusting this record on faith.
print3d: The silicone ashtray with lid is printable in TPU on a home printer, and this record gives the full directions, because TPU is the flexible filament that behaves most like silicone rubber. Print the dish and lid in 95A TPU, which is soft enough to seal and firm enough to hold its shape, with a 0.4 mm nozzle, a 0.2 mm layer height, 15 percent gyroid infill, and 4 perimeters, giving a wall about 1.6 mm thick. Use a direct-drive extruder if the printer has one, because TPU buckles in a long Bowden tube, and print at 25 to 30 mm per second, slower than rigid filament, with a first layer at 15 to 20 mm per second. Set the nozzle to 225 to 235 degrees C and the bed to 50 to 60 degrees C, with retraction at 0.8 mm and 25 mm per second, and the cooling fan at 50 percent. Print the dish upright on its base with no supports, and the lid flat on its face, also with no supports. Print time (estimate): about 2 hours 30 minutes for the dish and lid together at standard size. Post-processing is simple: remove any brim, check the 100 mm dish and the 104 mm lid with calipers, and wash the parts in warm soapy water before use. Unmodeled factors: wall thickness, supports, nozzle settings, printer motion, and material-specific slicing all change the real print time and strength, so the estimate is not a validated print job; measure the printed lip before trusting the seal. A printed TPU ashtray is a working copy, not a silicone original, and it should be checked for heat damage after its first use.
problem: The problem this supply solves is practical and narrow: silicone ashtray with lid needs to be prepared or used evenly, reliably, and with ordinary tools, without waste and without guesswork. Before a standard form existed, users improvised, and the result was uneven preparation, spilled material, and parts that wore out or broke. A good supply therefore has to do three things at once: hold the material securely, apply its mechanism evenly across the whole load, and survive repeated use without losing its shape or its edge. It also has to be easy to clean, because residue builds up and changes how it works, and easy to measure, because its dimensions set its capacity. This record states the problem in those terms so the specification, the science proof, and the mathematics can each be checked against it, and so a reader can judge whether the design in the record actually answers the problem it claims to solve.

"""The Silicone Ashtray with Lid — full working program.

Computes the same quantities as the record demo, as a documented module with a class and a run() method.
Run: python3 program.py
"""
import hashlib
import math


class SupplyCalculator:
    """Calculator for The Silicone Ashtray with Lid."""

    def compute(self):
        """Return the computed quantities as a dict."""
        d = 100.0; h = 28.0; wall = 4.0; lid_d = 104.0; lid_t = 5.0; rho = 1.15; cp = 1.46; dT = 200.0
        cap_mm3 = math.pi * ((d - 2.0 * wall) / 2.0) ** 2 * h
        cap_cm3 = cap_mm3 / 1000.0
        outer_mm3 = math.pi * (d / 2.0) ** 2 * (h + wall)
        body_cm3 = (outer_mm3 - cap_mm3) / 1000.0
        body_g = body_cm3 * rho
        lid_mm3 = math.pi * (lid_d / 2.0) ** 2 * lid_t
        lid_cm3 = lid_mm3 / 1000.0
        lid_g = lid_cm3 * rho
        total_g = body_g + lid_g
        heat_J = total_g * cp * dT
        return {"capacity_mm3": round(cap_mm3, 2), "capacity_cm3": round(cap_cm3, 2), "body_volume_cm3": round(body_cm3, 2), "body_mass_g": round(body_g, 2), "lid_volume_cm3": round(lid_cm3, 2), "lid_mass_g": round(lid_g, 2), "total_mass_g": round(total_g, 2), "heat_to_200C_J": round(heat_J, 2)}

    def run(self):
        """Compute twice, print named results and SHA-256 digests."""
        a = self.compute()
        b = self.compute()
        sa = hashlib.sha256(repr(sorted(a.items())).encode()).hexdigest()
        sb = hashlib.sha256(repr(sorted(b.items())).encode()).hexdigest()
        for key in sorted(a):
            print(f"{key}: {a[key]}")
        print(f"Run 1 SHA-256: {sa}")
        print(f"Run 2 SHA-256: {sb}")
        print(f"Deterministic: {'MATCH' if sa == sb else 'MISMATCH'}")
        return a


if __name__ == "__main__":
    SupplyCalculator().run()

use_program: To use the silicone ashtray with lid, set it on a flat surface, rest the cigarette or joint in a rim rest between draws, and tap ash into the dish. Close the lid when the session ends or when wind picks up, and the seal will keep ash in and smell down. Empty the dish when the ash reaches a third of the depth, while the embers are out, and wash it with warm soapy water or in a dishwasher, because silicone releases tar easily. Do not leave a lit ember pressed against one spot for a long time, even though silicone tolerates 230 degrees C, because a concentrated hot spot can scorch the surface. The program in this record computes what the dish holds and how it handles heat: the capacity from its diameter and depth, the body shell volume from the outer and inner cylinders, the lid volume from its diameter and thickness, the total mass from the silicone density, and the stored heat from the mass, the specific heat, and a 200 kelvin rise. Run the demo to see the numbers, then change one input at a time — a wider dish, a thicker lid, a deeper bowl — and watch the capacity and the total mass move. The program is the use check: if the lid volume it reports is far above the body volume, the lid is thicker than the record states, and the reader should re-measure the parts before trusting the seal.
